newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Dini says lira problems due to dollar.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Dini says lira problems due to dollar.

text.p: Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said on Wednesday that the lira's slide was due to the strength of the dollar and not to any doubt that Italy would be able to join European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).

"There are market dynamics regarding exchange rates that have nothing to do with our situation. Our situation has not changed from one day to the next. I think that overall it is improving," he told reporters.
Dini, a former central banker and prime minister, said the lira's slide was due to "a strong strengthening of the dollar, which is reflected on the mark as well as lira and sterling."
Dini, speaking on the sidelines of a foreign ministers' meeting about Turkey, was asked about rumours earlier on Wednesday of a delay in Italy's entry into EMU.
Asked if the rumours were a false alarm, he said: "absolutely."
Prime Minister Romano Prodi earlier rejected the rumours as "absurd".
Dini said the government was "fully committed to making every effort to be part of EMU from the start."
The Italian government has repeatedly reaffirmed Italy's intention to be among founder members of the euro from 1999. --Rome newsroom +396-678-2501
